source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 58: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions: this is collective-initialization scenario variant 58; launcher, backend and versions, expected world size, host placement, scheduler, container permissions, fabric, selected interfaces, GPU topology, and exact blocked stage are unknown. Measure them rather than infer them. Use an isolated diagnostic allocation, redact endpoints and credentials, and set a bounded watchdog with cleanup. Capture a run ID, host, rank/local-rank/world size, PID, launch configuration, software versions, rendezvous/store membership and timestamps, collective entry/exit and last-progress events, plus per-rank logs. Verify one process for every expected rank, unique membership and endpoint agreement, identical collective order, GPU visibility and rank-to-device mapping, driver/runtime compatibility, peer access, PCIe/NVLink topology, GPU health, container device access, ulimits/shared memory, selected NIC/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall, and transport errors.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-specific rendezvous membership or selected transport path defect prevents all participants from entering the same collective. Support requires repeatable rank/path-specific absence, late entry, or error and recovery after one authorized membership/interface correction; falsify it if all ranks enter over verified healthy paths while the hang persists. Run a minimal checksum all-reduce with an explicit timeout, recording per-rank entry/exit, checksum, latency, success, timeout, and error. Conduct repeated randomized matched trials for single-node, reduced-world, and full-world placements, changing one factor at a time (membership, interface, topology, or message size) and keeping software/configuration hashes fixed. Include a known-good control and separate denominators for success, timeout, rank failure, transport error, checksum mismatch, and cleanup failure.

Interpret cautiously: single-node or reduced-world success does not prove full-world fabric health; collective-order divergence, topology/GPU faults, software mismatch, resource limits, firewall/route/DNS/MTU issues, and intermittent failures are competing explanations. Gate any remedy on correct checksums, no rank loss, bounded timeout/cleanup, and agreed latency/SLO thresholds. Do not change production defaults or interfaces without authorization; canary first, preserve rollback configuration, terminate only the isolated job, and stop if diagnostics threaten production or evidence is contradictory. Evidence required includes redacted rank timelines, membership and rank-to-device maps, topology/GPU/driver/NIC/path outputs, repeated trial outcomes, and configuration hashes.
risks: A hang may instead arise from collective-order divergence, GPU/device/runtime faults, resource limits, or intermittent infrastructure.
Single-node or reduced-world success does not establish full-world network correctness; small samples can miss rare failures.
Interface changes and retries can affect production traffic without isolation, authorization, and bounded cleanup.
evidence_required: Redacted per-rank rendezvous and collective timelines; membership and rank-to-device mapping; topology, GPU, driver/runtime, NIC, route, and transport diagnostics; repeated randomized matched trials with checksums; separate outcome denominators and configuration hashes.

Interface changes and retries can affect production traffic without isolation, authorization, and bounded cleanup.
evidence_required: Redacted per-rank rendezvous and collective timelines; membership and rank-to-device mapping; topology, GPU, driver/runtime, NIC, route, and transport diagnostics; repeated randomized matched trials with checksums; separate outcome denominators and configuration hashes.
